doc.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021

title: Liner notes and reading DownBeat
summary: Rowe and Kirchner recall the experience of LPs and liner notes; Kirchner read DownBeat writers who later became friends.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: In retrospect, at the risk of sounding, you know, oh back in my day, there was something magical about finding these things. And you know you had a little transistor radio and saving up money to get LPs and then reading the liner notes as you listen to the record. It was like a whole experience.

Oh yeah. Yeah for sure. Well including the liner notes. I mean written by people like, well also I started reading DownBeat. You know I was reading all this stuff by people like Dan Morgenstern and Ira Gitler and Martin Williams, all of whom later became friends and colleagues of mine. So that was a big part of my education was reading this stuff that these people and others were writing at the time.
